svg.title: Why We Need Saving
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (Genesis 2:9, 16-17): the garden in Eden with fruit trees, a river, and one tree in the middle; God's voice speaks from above. Caption: "Eden. Every tree is good for food, and God gives the man one command." The LORD God says: "You may surely eat of every tree of the garden,". The LORD God says: "for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die." Panel 2 (Genesis 3:4-6): the tree in the middle of the garden, heavy with fruit, and the serpent at its foot with its head raised. Caption: "The serpent speaks to the woman." The serpent says: "You will not surely die. You will be like God." Genesis says: "the woman saw that the tree was good for food". Panel 3 (Genesis 3:8-10): the garden at evening, dark, with light falling on a thicket where the man and his wife are hiding; God's voice calls from above and the man answers from the thicket. Caption: "The cool of the day." The LORD God says: "Where are you?" The man says: "I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself." Panel 4 (Isaiah 53:6): six sheep scattered over open hills, near and far, each walking off in a different direction. Caption: "And every one of us since." Isaiah says: "All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned—every one—to his own way;". Panel 5 (Romans 5:8): three crosses on a rise under a dark sky, with no figures on them. Caption: "But God came looking." Paul says: "but God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us." The point: God's commands are for your good, and sin calls His good evil. Every one of us went our own way, but God came looking: while you were still a sinner, His Son Jesus died for you (Romans 5:8).
svg.text: Sin and the God who came looking, in one minute
God's commands are for your good, and sin calls His good evil.
Every one of us went our own way, but God came looking: while you
were still a sinner, His Son Jesus died for you (Romans 5:8).
No one is drawn in the garden: God gives no form there, and Adam and Eve are drawn only once He has
clothed them (Genesis 3:21). Genesis names no fruit and gives the serpent no shape before the curse.
